title: MSA/DPA + SLA & Billing alignment - BlueStone Retail vendor intake
summary: Kickoff to align on MSA and DPA redlines, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing models (committed vs pay-as-you-go), and procurement gating items. Primary blockers: indemnity cap, subprocessors list, SOC2 evidence timeline, and invoice cadence. Agreed to share full redline and security pack; pilot contract to be proposed by next Tuesday.
topics: SLA uptime, credits, and SLOs for dedicated pool
Billing models: committed monthly vs usage billing
SOC 2 / ISO evidence and penetration testing
Onboarding timeline and vendor gating checklist
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-21 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Sarah, Daniel, Priya, Marcus, Ana, Tom (BlueStone)

Summary / Context: BlueStone is evaluating Redwood for serving internal search & personalization models. Procurement has a tight Q4 onboarding window; legal needs indemnity/loss language clarified. Security needs SOC2 evidence and details on KMS/HSM and VPC options. Finance wants clear billing cadence and committed vs burst pricing.

[00:00] Maya (AE): okay hi everyone, thanks for carving time, i'm Maya from Redwood inference — quick roll call?
[00:08] Sarah (Procurement): Sarah here, procurement at BlueStone.
[00:11] Daniel (Legal): Daniel, legal counsel.
[00:13] Priya (ML): Priya, head of ML.
[00:15] Marcus (Security): Marcus, security.
[00:17] Ana (Finance): Ana, finance.
[00:18] Tom (Platform): Tom, platform eng.
[00:20] Liam (SE): Liam from Redwood, solutions engineering — hi all.

[00:32] Maya: quick agenda — MSA/DPA redlines, SLA and dedicated capacity questions, pricing models, and next steps, we can run 45-ish minutes then leave time for q's. sound good?
[00:40] Sarah: yes perfect.

[02:05] Daniel: to start, our legal team sent a redline earlier, main asks are: indemnity cap alignment to our enterprise caps, clarification on data processing for PII, and subprocessors list. we also need breach notification timing, usually 72 hours from detection.
[02:28] Maya: understood. redwood's standard MSA sets indemnity at a scaled cap, but we can look at your redline. we normally do 72 hours for notification except where regulated requires sooner, obviously we can escalate for sensitive data.
[02:46] Daniel: great. can you confirm insurance limits? our risk team will want to see the cgl and cyber liability numbers.
[02:53] Liam: yes we carry cyber and E&O; i'll send cert details — i have numbers now but i'll include them in the security pack.

[04:15] Marcus: on the security front, SOC 2 type II report — we need the full attestation and also pen-test summary. also, for key management, do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM in private deployments or only hosted?
[04:32] Liam: for Redwood Private (private control plane / VPC) customers can plug in their KMS — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM integrations in that mode. hosted API by default uses our managed keys but we offer a managed HSM for enterprise.
[04:54] Marcus: and what about auditing logs? we need audit trails forwarded to our SIEM and 90-day retention minimum.
[05:02] Maya: yes we have audit logs export — you can forward syslog to your collector in Private, and Dedicated also has a forwarding option. retention is configurable; we'll capture the standard but can extend via add-on.

[06:20] Priya: on the deployment side — we plan to start with a POC on hosted to validate latency then move to dedicated reserved capacity for production. what's your guaranteed latency SLO for dedicated pool?
[06:35] Liam: for dedicated we target p50/p95 40/120ms for typical 7B-class models with warm KV cache — but depends on sequence length and batching. we publish performance profiles per model.
[06:52] Priya: that aligns with our perf goals, but we need deterministic tail latency for user-facing search, otherwise we might use a smaller model for low-latency endpoints.
[07:03] Maya: we can recommend model variants and quantization to hit tail latency. also fallback routing to a cheaper model if the primary is degraded.

[08:15] Tom: curious on SLA credits — how are they calculated? p99 or availability? and what does a breach credit look like?
[08:28] Liam: our SLA is uptime-based per route for Dedicated: 99.95% monthly. credits scale: e.g., 99.95 to 99.0 gets 10% credit, below that larger credits; specifics in the SLA. credits are pro rata applied to invoice.
[08:46] Ana: pro rata is fine but we need predictable invoice adjustments — do credits apply to committed monthly fees or only usage?
[08:56] Maya: credits apply to the service fee line — for committed capacity it's applied against monthly reserved fee; for usage billing it's applied to usage charges. we'll show table in the SLA appendix.

[10:10] Sarah: procurement question: billing cadence, net terms? we run net 45 typical, some finance folks ask for net 60 for enterprise pilots. what's Redwood standard?
[10:24] Ana: (chimes) we prefer net 45; pilots might be prepaid credits.
[10:30] Maya: our public terms are net 30, but for enterprise deals we do net 45 on approved credit; net 60 requires credit review. pilots often use upfront credits or a small committed minimum.
[10:45] Daniel: on termination and data after termination — we need guaranteed data deletion timelines and proof of deletion for customer data in Hosted mode.
[10:55] Liam: for Private/Dedicated, you control retention. For Hosted we have deletion procedures and can provide certificate of deletion for customer data, typical time is 30 days but can be negotiated.

[12:03] Marcus: subprocessors — we need the full list and if any subprocessor operates outside EU/US or does support engineering from third-party vendors. also data residency questions — our europa customers must remain in eu region.
[12:20] Maya: we'll share subprocessors spreadsheet. we support region pinning for data residency in Hosted zones (EU region) and Dedicated/Private runs in customer's VPC / region. some managed services may be in US but access controls apply.

[13:40] Daniel: indemnity cap — your redline sets cap at direct damages only; our standard is a higher cap for breaches involving PI. can we consider an elevated cap for security incidents?
[13:55] Maya: we can consider a carve-out for security incidents, subject to our insurance limits — we'll need to confirm exact cap numbers with legal.

[15:10] Priya: shifting away slightly — model governance: can we run evals and get model fingerprints or hashes so we can track regressions after rollouts? this is important for experiment reproducibility.
[15:25] Liam: yes our rollout tooling includes model versioning and fingerprint metadata; we can export model artifacts and kv cache snapshots for evals. note: some labels can be stripped in hosted mode; for Dedicated/Private you get more artifact access.

[16:50] Sarah: procurement gating checklist — what docs do we need to unblock onboarding?
[16:58] Maya: typically: signed MSA, DPA, security pack (SOC2, pen test summary), subprocessors list, insurance cert, SSO/SAML integration plan, and billing terms. we can prepare a vendor onboarding packet.
[17:15] Sarah: timeline — we need vendor approved by start of Q4, ideally by Oct 1st. can you commit to that cadence?
[17:24] Maya: yes, assuming redline turnaround 2 weeks and security review 1 week, pilot contract internal approvals, it's doable.

[18:40] Daniel: one technical legal ask — source code escrow? for critical models we sometimes require escrow of critical components. is that supported?
[18:52] Liam: we don't escrow model weights by default; for enterprise private deployments we can discuss escrow of the serving runtime binaries or packaging under a separate agreement. i'll flag that for our legal ops.

[20:05] Marcus: can you confirm data in motion encryption and in rest encryption details? also TLS versions and cipher suites?
[20:14] Liam: TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred. data at rest is AES-256. Private supports customer KMS. we'll include cipher suite details in the security pack.

[21:45] Priya: about pricing constructs — we have three buckets: experiment (low usage), pilot (predictable but small), and production (high, predictable). what's recommended billing mix?
[21:58] Maya: recommended: experiment on hosted pay-as-you-go to iterate; pilot convert to short committed reserved capacity to hit predictable MOL, then production on dedicated reserved with monthly commit for cost predictability. we also offer burst credits for traffic spikes.

[23:20] Ana: how do you calculate token billing across multiple models and function calls? we have a lot of short calls; we need per-route, per-model cost breakdown in invoice.
[23:35] Liam: invoices can be itemized per route/model. token accounting follows prompt + completion tokens; function/tool calls are charged per token consumed by the model. we also support aggregated monthly reports and per-token cost allocation.

[25:00] Tom: is there a minimum committed spend for dedicated pools? and how flexible is resizing?
[25:10] Maya: minimum depends on capacity size — typical entry is equivalent to a small dedicated pool (~$20k/month) but we can structure pilot-friendly low-commit tiers. resizing can be done monthly; autoscaling handles short bursts.

[26:40] Sarah: procurement: can discounts be structured as rebate vs list price reductions? finance prefers net net reductions to simplify accounting.
[26:52] Ana: rebates create more accounting churn.
[26:56] Maya: we can do list price reduction in the contract for committed volumes — rebates are also possible but we'll work with finance on preferred structure.

[28:10] Daniel: licensing language — do you have restrictions on model outputs or indemnity for generated IP claims? we need assurance on training data provenance.
[28:25] Liam: we have usage policies and indemnity for egregious IP claims is limited; training data provenance differs by model — for Redwood-curated open models we provide provenance notes; for third-party models we list origins when available. we'll include IP guidance in the DPA appendix.

[30:02] Priya: what's the onboarding plan for SSO and SAML? we have Okta, SCIM provisioning — how long to set up?
[30:12] Liam: SAML + SCIM common setup can be done in 3-5 business days for Hosted with guidance, longer if custom attribute mapping. Dedicated/Private provides deeper integration. we'll run a tech onboarding workshop.

[31:30] Marcus: regarding access controls — can you do role-based access with per-token tracing and audit? we want to link tokens to users and trace calls for compliance.
[31:44] Liam: yes RBAC with audit trails is supported; per-token tracing is part of the console — we can show sample traces. note: in hosted mode PII in traces is masked by default.

[33:05] Maya: i'd like to propose a path: we'll share a redline response and full security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, subprocessors, certs) by Friday. we'll draft a pilot contract (one month, small commit) for your legal to review.
[33:20] Sarah: timeline and owners?
[33:26] Maya: owner for Redwood: Maya (contract & pricing), Liam (technical security). BlueStone owners: Daniel (legal), Marcus (security), Sarah/Ana (procurement/finance).

[34:45] Daniel: one more clause — data subject access requests (DSARs) handling and timelines; we need explicit cooperation commitments.
[34:58] Liam: we have a DSAR process, we commit to assist and provide logs and exports for a customer's DSAR within statutory timelines; will include text in DPA.

[36:10] Priya: performance benchmarking — can we run a standardized benchmark (we have a 1k-user replay) and have Redwood run it on your dedicated infra to validate performance & cost estimates?
[36:25] Liam: yes, we can run a benchmarking pass. we'll need the dataset replay and target models; we can run it on dedicated pool and provide token-level breakdown and perf profile.

[37:50] Tom: for monitoring, is there an option to integrate Prometheus metrics or push metrics to datadog?
[37:58] Liam: yes, we can forward metrics to Datadog or Prometheus endpoints for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has metric export via webhooks and we can export aggregated metrics.

[39:10] Ana: invoicing detail — can we get line items for committed vs burst usage, and a forecast?
[39:22] Maya: yes we provide forecast exports and detailed invoices monthly; we can create custom billing CSVs for internal chargebacks.

[40:48] Sarah: what's the signoff criteria for procurement approving vendor?
[40:55] Sarah (cont): legal signoff on MSA/DPA, security signoff on SOC2 and KMS plan, finance on billing cadence and commit. once those are green we'll route for vendor gate.

[42:12] Daniel: regarding redlines — we'll mark a few high-priority ones: induction of arbitration clause, liability cap, and breach notification timing. if Redwood can accept or propose alternative language we can move quickly.
[42:28] Maya: yes we'll propose compromise language for arbitration and propose a limited carve-out for security incidents per insurance limits.

[44:05] Priya: technical Q — can we get per-model token budgets and throttles per route so we can enforce cost controls?
[44:15] Liam: yes Rate limits and per-route token budgets are configurable; Console has budget alerts and automatic throttling policies.

[45:40] Maya: ok to wrap — quick recap and next steps.
[45:46] Maya: Redwood actions: 1) send formal redline response and marked-up MSA by Friday, 2) share security pack and subprocessors list by Friday, 3) draft pilot contract for 30-day pilot with small commit by next Tuesday, 4) schedule technical benchmark session (Liam to schedule)
[46:10] Daniel: BlueStone actions: 1) review redline & security pack, 2) confirm internal vendor gating timeline, 3) provide dataset replay for benchmarking if pilot approved.

[47:30] Sarah: any blockers on signatures? none from procurement side if legal/security align.
[47:40] Maya: great. we'll send links to the docs and a calendar invite for the benchmark.

[49:00] Ana: quick finance note — please include PO number flow details and tax handling in the pilot contract.
[49:10] Maya: will do.

[50:20] Marcus: one final ask — can we have a 1:1 security deep dive after you send the pack? maybe 60 minutes next week.
[50:30] Liam: yes, we'll set that up — propose dates in the invite.

[51:05] Maya: cool thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the packet and next steps.
[51:12] Priya: thanks all.
[51:15] Daniel: thanks.
[51:17] Sarah: thanks.
[51:20] (meeting ends)
